# PR #550 / issue #363 final audit

**CHANGES_REQUIRED** at head `55c9a5497f9e4a6e7f9ebeaa29283e3898170683`, tree `1108c458b590bbfedfcf3a5e39b1966eb8252e62`, against signed main `a84f988b89e456b0e2270e3c4750afb250b6c68f`. **Formal scan 3 of 3.** The Windows product correction meets the measured 226-character criterion. One introduced race in its maintained abort regression can fail a correct build and bypass cancellation of a fixture child.

## F3 · P2 · Publish a complete readiness record before the abort observer reads it

The new CLI fixture writes JSON directly to the final readiness path at `schema-cli.mjs` lines 11–21. Concurrently the host polls for the path, immediately parses its contents at line 48, and calls `controller.abort()` at line 51. The supported Node v22.23.4 string write opens the named file with flag `w`, writes its contents in a later filesystem operation and then closes it. The file already exists between the open and the write. A concurrent poll can therefore read an empty file and throw a JSON parse error before cancellation. The CLI’s abort mode holds an interval indefinitely. A failure on this path can also leave the helper running if it has reached that wait. Both processes can follow their normal code paths for this to occur. [Writer at the reviewed head](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/55c9a5497f9e4a6e7f9ebeaa29283e3898170683/packages/adapter-codex/src/fixtures/schema-cli.mjs#L11-L33) · [Reader and abort at the reviewed head](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/blob/55c9a5497f9e4a6e7f9ebeaa29283e3898170683/packages/adapter-codex/src/fixtures/sdk-schema-case.mjs#L44-L54) · [Pinned Node implementation, open and write](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v22.23.4/src/node_file.cc#L2455-L2475)

Publish the record atomically, for example by writing and closing a uniquely named sibling and renaming it to the marker path. Ensure an observer failure also aborts and settles the owned work. A focused check can pause before publication, verify that the reader continues waiting, then release the writer and verify that the reader observes valid JSON, aborts and reaps the helper. Preserve the existing schema, sentinels and cleanup assertions.

This is a static finding from both fixture blobs and the exact runtime implementation. The historical runs reviewed here recorded successful maintained regressions. I did not observe an instance of the race or an orphan in those runs. The source witness and exact Node file hash are in `marker-race-source.json`.

## Product and integration

- At `76beeb0f` the adapter switched to cryptographic four-byte random names, exclusive nonrecursive `mkdir` with requested mode `0700`, and four total attempts. Only `EEXIST` permits a retry. Cleanup starts from successful ownership and preserves the existing cancellation and error precedence. Request/configured working directories still bypass allocation.
- At corrected source `7d8467439b9850a555b92ab4b96b58c8b8b78388`, D177 shortened the pinned SDK’s host schema prefix to `gg-schema-`. I verified the adapter-resolved SDK bytes against the original with only that literal replaced. The installed SDK SHA-256 is `ec7471535be310cabbb8f256faa80a1101e46b84b41d42cae40a3e36a9a5feb7`. Native exclusive creation, schema serialization, lifecycle cleanup and the existing `windowsHide` hunk are preserved. The three lock entries are an exact hash substitution. The patch SHA-256 is `119554c3f7cb39db6b24dbb75e9d51fede75171d04aec0114d31356b79693760`. The pinned package version, Apache-2.0 license and public dependency configuration match the baseline.
- The current head’s ordinary parents are archive child `6216b9a1397642ae522908ded008f3229608eab8` and target `a84f988b89e456b0e2270e3c4750afb250b6c68f`. The seven runtime, test, fixture, patch and lock blobs match the corrected source. The only incoming package changes are the two #547 JSDoc edits, byte-identical to target. Removing the JSDoc blocks yields byte-identical executable source on both sides. All three saved merge stages for each conflict match Git. The final attributes, ignore rules and changelog preserve both parents’ content. The worktree and index were clean.
- The docs/06 length sentence has direct support in the separate full adapter/SDK harmless-CLI author replay for success, error and abort. The maintained real-SDK unit suite specifically checks the 243/255 schema lengths, the allocator suite checks the 249-character scratch, and independent native QA checks all three on success. ADR-0087 identifies these tiers. The optional wording refinement does not affect this verdict. The pre-existing ADR-0086 index omission and unused older SDK installation do not affect the resolved package.

## Independent QA and review

| Record | Independently checked result |
| --- | --- |
| Original allocator | 18 candidate controls and one expected baseline failure control passed. The independent Windows run used the actual filesystem and a local harness, including a real Node cwd child, real collision failures, four-attempt exhaustion, ordinary failure, directory precedence, abort and cleanup precedence. |
| Original SDK boundary | The original driver remains **0/2**. Its whole-temp assertion counted a tsx cache. The retained short call reaches the harmless CLI. The long call allocates the adapter scratch, then fails with `ENAMETOOLONG` at the old SDK schema prefix before the turn. Both scratches are removed. |
| Correction author | The old-prefix counterfactual records one failure and five skipped cases. The corrected focused suites record **57 passed**. Six full adapter/SDK harmless-CLI cases passed. The Windows adapter suite records **675 passed, four live skips, 99.41% lines and 95.50% branches**. The first lint run’s 16 errors remain in the packet and the corrected run passed. |
| Corrected independent SDK | D183 accepts eight intended scenarios across 12 calls. The original driver remains **0/8**. Its pre-spawn argument filter missed child observations. Two original abort fixtures fell through to a nonexistent Node main and were excluded. The four original harmless success/error outcomes, schema contents and filesystem states are retained. |
| Native Windows success | Corrected native short and long calls passed **2/2** through the public adapter, default harness, installed SDK and bundled `codex.exe`. Both turn processes exited 0, each sent one strict-schema request to the synthetic loopback Responses endpoint, and the returned proofs, cleanup and three sentinels matched. The 226-character case observed lengths **249 / 243 / 255**, PID 27004. Four native calls occurred in total across the original and corrected pairs. |
| Harmless CLI abort | The corrected abort driver remains **0/2** because the SDK removed the listener before its exit callback. Both saved states show scratch and schema present at cancellation, public `AbortError`, a `SIGTERM` handle result, empty live handles, subsequent cleanup and preserved sentinels. The last scoped CIM observation found none of 32 recorded PIDs or matching node/codex command lines under three fixture roots. Native Codex error/abort and real provider entitlement remain unverified. |

The implementation author identifies its SDK context as `/root/i4_448_preflight`, GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh. The independent QA context used separate checkouts and separate fixtures. Its Sol xhigh identity is coordinator-dispatch/continuation evidence. The original SDK-boundary evaluator has no independently attested model envelope. The two Claude reviews each have a distinct actual provider session, a terminal event identical to the result, nonzero `claude-opus-5-5` usage, xhigh launch configuration and process exit 0. The current auditor is a fresh configured GPT-6.2 Astra MAX context, with no separate provider identity attestation.

Slot 1 remains **CHANGES_REQUIRED** at `76beeb0f`, SHA-256 `efab11b92aa1f406d9d53eef4334b05cca4de1f485293d851a173246b3d6949a`. Slot 2 is **ACCEPT CORRECTION** for F1 and F2 at `7d846743`, SHA-256 `1c01ec92fbd9e526c35366781824c3f27890a43148dfb345a8c82cd99f982993`. I compared the exact bytes of both public comment bodies with their terminal reports. I also checked the identical public issue/PR QA summaries, CI publication and separate corrective review context. GitHub records these as ordinary issue comments. Its PR-review and review-thread lists were empty. [Slot 1](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/550#issuecomment-7061290665) · [Slot 2](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/550#issuecomment-7061723533) · [PR QA](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/550#issuecomment-7061310292) · [Issue QA](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/issues/363#issuecomment-7061311002)

## CI, archive and disposition

GitHub returned six successful jobs on run **44894502596, attempt 1**. The tested synthetic merge is `7dafb6a54586928199c95c7170780378b5036e19`, with parents main then PR head and the reviewed tree. Original logs yield **10,049 unit passes, 52 skips, 488 browser passes, 27 native Windows passes, and 22 successful coverage tasks**. The coverage artifact contains 13 package summaries, each above 90% on all four metrics. The repository job passed its frozen install, build, acceptance suites, typecheck, lint, format, layer/dependency, migration, design-token, template, licensing, generated-doc and audit steps. The dependency audit reported seven low and 13 moderate findings and zero high or critical findings. The conditional browser failure upload was skipped on success. [CI run](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/actions/runs/44894502596) · [CI publication](https://github.com/Jacob-J-Thomas/GraphGoblin/pull/550#issuecomment-7061548828)

The downloaded Windows artifact **14703338512** matches the live GitHub SHA-256 `357d01a5ba9ad144cb84974be96a8b4013ac17ddfc5500ad7f10c4ac3f4d0b61`. Its three members match the retained corpus and all three stored replay files byte-for-byte. I checked the sequence and type counts of 338 records, the exact checkout, the matching replay-helper source, and zero rejected or omitted records. This is CI launcher evidence. The issue-specific native CLI proof comes from the independent QA rows above. The early coordinator verifier `FileNotFoundError` occurred before the artifact was available. The original CI run and artifact were used throughout.

All **339 #363 blobs** and **243 inherited #547 blobs** match their original commits. The #363 archive contains 6,127,574 bytes. Its outer seal covers 338 members and has SHA-256 `52c70ecbd34de5db3fa65257d0679078a6087047ff2ec69d79b61b90f7dc5bb1`. The 329 selected originals totaling 5,840,963 bytes match their external sources, with zero omitted original members. I verified six nested manifests covering 330 entries with overlap, 46 external source/fixture bindings, 13 source-freeze entries, 25 explicitly tracked ignored logs and the 49-member integration seal. The later `root-freeze.py` is separately mapped coordinator material. The stopped pre-push preflight is retained. Bounded checks of the added blobs found zero matches for the specified token, key and JWT patterns. The archive intentionally contains local paths, fixture identifiers, process IDs and synthetic endpoint evidence. This check gives no general secret-scanning assurance.

Live issue #363 is open and eligible for engineering delivery under `aidlc-ready` and `qa:touched-systems`. The issue has no native parent, no human/parking/plan label and no issue-specific owner closure hold in its body or three comments. PR #550 is draft/open, refers to #279 as “Part of,” and names only #363 in GitHub’s closing references. **The final gate is held for F3.** The three general slots are consumed. The coordinator owns the existing bounded correction procedure, any subsequent exact-head/current-target CI, and signed integration. #363 remains open. The separate #448/#459 owner QA, Mac #501, held #460 and consolidated owner acceptance retain their own gates.

Verification used immutable Git blobs, original saved logs/states and artifact bytes, and fresh read-only GitHub metadata. I performed no product, behavior, CI or provider execution and no product/index/ref or GitHub mutation. Detailed checks are in `source-evidence-binding.json`, `live-github-binding.json` and `marker-race-source.json`.
